en: With a lightning form; [and] in a former form, as the four Vedas
as lamplight; as the moon itself which appearing rises
As a later form, [and] as one without birth
who was without old age [or] disease in a former form
A golden form which is valued [and] without being intended for ever dying; in a jeweled form
as the five elements; in the form of water; the shining light in a fire form
As his own form, my father, who remains in my form
[his] sacred [tender] sprout-like feet are on my head
When considering the sacred forms of the celestials [as] different
who remain called the Three in beautiful forms
Which remain pervasive as the many various creeds
[and] being the wide earth, water, fire, wind, and the sky
When seeing [these] three forms which endure
one form is golden, one form is red fire, and one like the form of the dark sea -
The light that is One is the form of our god of the cloud-[like] form
A perception cannot exist of one shape, of one appearance
of the dark blue-hued one
Of our Lord, saying he glowed the color of a [white] conch
at the time he took nectar from the sea in a huge shape
Saying in [his] sacred shape is dark, tall Māl
calling [him] ‘the red one’ in the Trēta [Yuga]
Say who is able to see him of the dark form with red eyes
without always praising [him] in era to era!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: The Primal [Lord] for Indra and Brahma, the Brahman
who is inconceivable [even] for the gods in heaven
Being the vast earth, wind, fire, water, the heavens, [and] the five senses
being the fine, elegant sound of Tamil [and] northern words
Being the four quarters, being the sun and moon
[he who is] the mantra kept [in] the Brahmins’ twilight prayers -
If you always praise [him] with [this] mantra, not forgetting [a word]
we can prosper, simple heart
Entering into the water in a beautiful step, as one foot remained
one foot, surpassing the thoughts conceived in the mind
Of the demon of enviable wealth, going above the cosmic egg
rising into the vast heavens, racing higher
As it left [behind] the cool moon and the rayed [sun]
brushing the back of the stars [and] surpassing that region
I bow to the flower-like sacred feet of our father
who [thus] encompassed the whole world
Singing of his feet in all of the cities in which he rejoices
the celestials’ king of long, broad hands which grant enough [to satisfy]
The single rider on the beautiful winged bird
the man with a merciless nature who always gives trouble to demons -
[My] heart, go forth; let us worship [him in] lush Kōvalūr with pond borders
where wealth is grown, as water spreads over the fields
While many pearls burst from tall bamboo
dragged by the turbid Peṇṇai [River] which comes spreading [over] the ground
[My] heart, go forth; let us worship [him] in lush Kōvalūr
with lotus borders on long streets surrounded by fragrant groves
Which endures for the king of [the people of] the magnificent mountains to worship
where the chaste, simple virgin who dwells in the Vindhyas
Undertook protection of the city of him who, ruling the world bearing a curved axe
so that kings with strong mountain[-like], high shoulders would die
Conquered first [among others] the youth who threw
a singular spear in the wide sea with mountains
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: You of Nīrakam, you who is on the peak of a high mountain
of Nilāttinkaḷtuṇṭam, and of Ūrakam in prosperous Kacci
You who is in Veḵkā with glittering harbor waters
you in the hearts of those who think [of you]
You of Kārakam, which the world praises, in Kārvāṉam, O thief
you within Pēr established on the south side of the lush, desirable Kāviri
You who is in my heart without leaving
Great Lord, [in all of these] I cherished your divine feet
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: You of Mallai of the ocean where huge jewels, coming by ship, cast up
you of the city of walled Kacci, of Pēr
You whose half is he whose chest has a garland with fertile cassia full of nectar
he who bears at his left side the innocent girl of the man of the mountain range
You of the Sea of Milk, you on earth
you of the cool mountain peak, O coral-hued One
Where have you appeared [now], our great Lord?
I, a wretch, searching for you, wander [aimlessly] like this
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: Golden elephant, glorious elephant engaged in guarding the seven gardens!
I am a contemptuous slave!
Except to call “My elephant! My elephant!”
as a simpleton, what do I know?
Worshipped by the world, [you are] the elephant of the south, the elephant of the north
the elephant of the west side, [and] the rutting elephant who is in the east
You are always at the fore of the gods; you are the splendor of Tirumūḻikkaḷam
adored by those who come after; you are the First
gloss: perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person
perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person
perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: Neglecting the clothes that she wears, [this] girl, who weeps, cares not
she does not sleep as the tears of [her] elongated, moist eyes overflow
She who cannot sit on my lap for the tiniest length of time
keeps asking, “Where is Tiruvaraṅkam of our Lord?”
As a soothsayer said words truthfully to us [of] who did this
to [this] simple girl with tresses where jewel[-like] bees hum, choking on nectar
She said, “O Ladies, the sea-hued one did this
Who will protect her [now]?”
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: She stands [stricken] as her eyes stream, her heart melting; she languishes
she sighs at length; she ignores food [and] cares not [for] sleep
I begot this girl who says, “Noble who rests [in yogic] sleep on the poisonous snake,”
who says, “Young man of Āli with fields of flowers full of fragrance,”
Who says, “Friend, shall we dance in ornate Araṅkam
where they dance [and] sing of the banner with a fine winged bird,”
And who is not restrained under my wing
I gained the blame of [all of] those in the vast world. Alas!
Saying, “Lifting a hill, you protected [the herd] from hailstones,”
saying, “You of Ūrakam in Kacci with desirable flowers,”
Saying, “Breaking a bow, you embraced the shoulders of [her who is] soft in nature,”
saying, “King who lies sleeping in Veḵkā,”
Saying, “Wrestling, you destroyed the wrestlers that day,”
saying, “My young man with hands that split [the mouth of] the horse,”
Uttering [these] words, saying, “Speak” to her parakeet
she languishes as [tear]drops trickle on both of her breasts
Listening as [it] sings of [the sun’s] burgeoning rays, the cloud in Kuṟuṅkuṭi
the unfathomable, rare nectar who endures as the First
Surpassing the three worlds that do not age [and] beyond that
the Brahman who dwells in Araṅkam
Of him who is the thoughts of the brahmins, lamplight
the emerald in Tiruttaṇkā, Tirumāl of Veḵkā
Saying, “By raising [you], I received [my] reward. Come,”
joining her hands [in prayer], she bowed to her innocent parakeet
Saying, “[Bull] elephant who dwells in Kacci encircled by tall walls where stones rise,”
saying, “[Sweet] ripe fruit who lies in the sea,”
Saying, “Lord who rejoices standing in ornate Aḻuntūr
with borders of fields with ponds of lily flowers,”
[Thus] bearing on her breast a long vīṇā where tones rise
smiling, as her teeth appear slightly [in] a pure smile
Playing so that her soft fingers become red
like a soft parakeet, my foolish [girl] babbles profusely
Saying, “Youth who sweetly rejoiced, having grazed the calves,”
saying, “My [sweet] ripe fruit of Kaṇṇapūram girded by fragrant groves,”
Saying, “You who was happy dancing the wooden [stilt] dance [in] the village commons,”
saying, “Young man who dwells in Tiruvēṅkaṭam [in] the north,”
Saying, “King who defeated and weeded out the demon clan,”
saying, “You who stands in Tirunaṟaiyūr girded by spreading groves,”
Saying, “My friend of dark color [and] thick curls,”
she languishes as tear[drops] trickle on both of her breasts
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, second person, vocative
participial noun, perfective aspect, second person, vocative

en: As her soft, heaving, young breasts grow pallid
and tears keep on springing forth [from] her eyes, like opposing fish
Thinking [of him], her body melting at the little coo
which the rosy-legged, simple dove sounds for [his] hen
Singing there of Taṇkāl and the cool city of Kuṭantai
singing of cool Kōvalūr
Listening as she dances, when [I] say, “Girl, is this good for our family?”
she [still] practices, she who [then] sings of Naṟaiyūr, too!
I [must have] committed a sin against the Lady of the dewy blossom
of the mad one who is [also] devoted to the simple maiden whose form is the earth
[Of the one with] a body the the color of rainclouds
and lotus-colored eyes, mouth, palms, and both feet
My foolish [girl] of beautiful figure doesn’t hear my words
She says, “Where is our Lord’s Tiruvaraṅkam?”
She says, “I’ll go to the sea-hued one’s Nīrmalai.”
Isn’t this the way those whose perfection was ruined remain?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person
perfective aspect, participial noun, third person

en: As soon as seeing that the girl with unmatured, beautiful breasts
will be the one on Māyaṉ’s strong chest
She was thus. She, whose perfection was ruined, sighs
she says, “Friend, shall we dance in ornate Araṅkam?”
As I who begot [her] speak, she does not hear a single word [from my] mouth!
Singing of Pēr [and] singing of the cool city of Kuṭantai
She has gone to bathe in Golden Lotus tank
[Ladies,] my girl is without comparison; are your golden [girls] also [like] that?
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, first person, singular

en: [This] girl who chants the names of the renowned one
who rules the world, having dug up [that] world, eaten the world
Spit out the world [again and] measured the world
[of] the man of war who, having kindled a hot blaze so that Lanka to the south
Once trembled to end the wealth of the sword[-bearing] demon who mastered the chariot
as the ruler of the world flourished having traversed the defenses
Of the crashing seas [and] entered [Śoṇitapura] to end [the life of] thousand-armed Bāṇa
besides calling [her] the great[est] ascetic on earth, can one speak [at all]?
As a lock of fragrant kohl-colored curls hung at the back
[and] as earrings with makara danced, shining at both sides
[With] only an arrow-worthy cruel bow as [his] companion
they both came here and stood before me
The color of his hands, [like] lotuses, a lotus[-like] mouth
and lotuses - both eyes - and feet, too, were that
Even though we saw the reality of him [with] such beauty, friend
thinking him a “god,” we were frightened
While exploring one hill melody and while glancing at us
as if he were a bit shy, then
In the time that [he] performed a love[song]
as my heart and eyes, rushing, reached the sacred feet of our Lord
After that, I did not see my bangles and sash
[but] I did see his thick makara earrings and four arms
To me who asked, “How far is our Lord’s temple?”
he said, “Isn’t this it, lovely Āli?”
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, first person, singular, dative

en: Giving to me mental anguish that seeped inside
he took my bright bangles and dark coloring
I see in a place of dream
him of the fresh tulasī garland where nectar seeps
As [he] says, “Our city is Tiruvaraṅkam, here where carp leap
drinking seeping, clarified toddy [made from] young coconut fruit”
When I see him, I say, “You bird-riding thief, don’t go!”
Nevertheless, this is [just] pique to us
These conch [bangles] on both arms will not stay; Poor me!
He whose color is like a big-bellied dark cloud
Who ate, forcing in the great seas with shining, roaring waters
he, whose great mouth consumed the world, coming here
Bearing in one hand the conch and in the other hand the discus
as great ascetics [and] sages of harsh austerities circled [him]
As my opposing fish eyes welled with tears, he went
saying “[My] city is Araṅkam in the river” [and] making me sulk
[After] revealing [his] sacred form flashing like lightning, his broad shoulders
hands that raged at an elephant, his eyes and lips
And earrings with makara that flash, hanging below
[his chaplet of] fragrant, flowering tulasī
Taking my virtue, my perfection, my thoughts
and my bangles, taking me as [his] slave
He went saying, “[My] city is Araṅkam in the river
midst groves of fragrant gold-blossomed campaka.”
Spotless, [pollen]-filled, six-legged little bee
you and your lady sitting sweetly clasping a flower
Your mouth sipping the nectar
of a blossomed bush in a honey-filled garden
I honor you! Going now to him who stands in ornate Aḻuntūr
the immortals’ king who grazed the herd, cherishing the cows
Approaching [and] staying [there] without fear, uttering briefly
“A lady loves you,” see [what happens]
Simple, red-legged heron, going now
entering blessed Kaṇṇapuram, if you were to speak
To my red-eyed Māl, my love, my friend
there would be no [other] delight like this for us
When all of this lush land becomes yours forever
I will give fish in the fields to eat, having caught [them]
If [I] give [that], you and your lady, coming here [and] staying happily
may happily experience delights in this vast land
[That] massive mountain-shaped bull elephant who drove a chariot
to end the great, renowned Bhārata [War]
Wandering the three worlds, arriving so that the demon died
scattering the defenses of southern Lanka
Friend, as one who is without strength [to keep him] from going
[by] clasping [him] to the mounds of my breasts of pallid glow
Reaching a pique, [but] thinking of [him] always so that delight reaches [me]
arriving [in] every limb on me, I am tender[-hearted]
gloss: imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: Once king to the maids of the cowherd clan
the Lord who dammed, having churned, the crashing sea
He who was victorious, expelling the [demon] clan, discharging that arrow from a curved bow
to kill the demons’ king of undiminishing strength
He whose arms bore a mountain, he who always stands embracing
Viṇṇakaram with vast rolling waters
Māl who lies in cool Kuṭantai, the tall One -
I, a slavish cur, am obsessed with [him]
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person

en: Those who master [this] garland of Tamil, [this well-]crafted text composed by Kaliyaṉ
strong, spear[-wielding] Parakālaṉ
King of Maṅkai of enduring, jeweled great mansions
to [our] Father who, as a swan, revealed the rare Mysteries
As immortals along with sages praised [him], saying
“You the hue of clouds which creep [through]
The dark, flashing rains, great Lord of celestials, have mercy!”
they will be able to cut the roots of their ancient sins of old
